question.problem:
Consider the binomial random variable $X∼B(6,0.26).$ Rounding to $4$ decimal places, fill in the missing values in the cumulative distribution function table below.

| $\,x\,$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $P(X\le x)$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | $\,0.8144\,$ | $\,0.9569\,$ | $\,0.9944\,$ | $\,0.9997\,$ | $\,1.0000\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

The probability mass function for the Binomial distribution $B(n,p)$ is given by

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},\,x=0,1,2,…,n.
$$

In our case, $n=6$ and $p=0.26.$ 

Therefore, we compute the missing elements of the table as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(0) & =P(X\le 0) \\  & =P(X=0) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{0})(0.26)^{0}(1-0.26)^{6-0} \\  & =1\cdot (0.26)^{0}\cdot (0.74)^{6} \\  & ≈0.1642.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1) & =P(X\le 1) \\  & =P(X=0)+P(X=1) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{0})(0.26)^{0}(1-0.26)^{6-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{1})(0.26)^{1}(1-0.26)^{6-1} \\  & =1\cdot (0.26)^{0}\cdot (0.74)^{6}+6\cdot (0.26)^{1}\cdot (0.74)^{5} \\  & ≈0.5104.\end{aligned}
$$
